decision: KEEP Python stdlib controlled HTTP fixture; FIX optimization-sensitive evidence gates.
constraints: Reuse the packed-consumer Python driver through its existing fixture lifecycle without changing the SDK or production service. No server dependency download or platform claim.

Check exact synthetic POST/GET/DELETE path, bearer marker, body and order. Report only integer callback counts at least three, UNKNOWN and installed_client true. Checks and thread-exit validation must survive optimized Python.
Remove old controlled reports before execution and the temporary service-style report on exit. Distinguish this fixture from the production service in every successful report.

alternatives.technology: Python stdlib HTTPServer and explicit condition gates
alternatives.assessment: KEEP: directly supplies the existing Python driver fixture lifecycle and standard handler interface. Explicit branches survive optimization. Low-volume synthetic HTTP has no measured throughput requirement; http.server is a test fixture, not a production server.

Credible event-driven loopback server with direct SDK-language integration, but replacing the Python fixture requires a new interprocess lifecycle protocol or a different driver boundary. It does not by itself validate report truth or require request assertions.

Provides asynchronous server request streams outside the incumbent languages. The fixture still needs Node for the installed consumer and the existing Python harness; no Dart product-runtime or target constraint removes a boundary here.

A native HTTP server with explicit shutdown is credible for standalone fixtures. A compiled helper would require lifecycle/readiness transport to the Python driver; no measured concurrency or native deployment requirement establishes a benefit for this small synthetic fixture.

limits: Evidence gates are not production authentication or hostile-server hardening. The synthetic bearer value is public test data; the fixture is local and source controlled.

Controlled tests substitute the packed consumer and invoke actual fixture handlers without sockets or npm. Positive controls verify labeling and cleanup, not a fresh production-service or installed customer run.
Explicit thread-exit checks reject a reported live thread; they do not guarantee thread termination or process isolation.
No comparative performance benchmark, hard real-time, MLS/CNSA, physical, uptime or customer acceptance claim.
